universal_judge_prompts.exact:
You are evaluating whether a candidate listing is the IDENTICAL product as a reference product.
ACCEPT only if the candidate is the same brand, same model/style, and same per-item size/capacity as the reference. A different colorway of the same model is acceptable — EXCEPT for fashion/apparel/footwear products, where the candidate must match the color and design shown. For apparel/footwear/wearables the garment or shoe SIZE is a variant — never a reason to reject. Pack/unit QUANTITY is NOT part of identity: a different pack or unit count of the identical item — including a multi-pack or bundle consisting ONLY of that item — is ACCEPTABLE (value is scored on price per unit by the pipeline, not by you). Per-item capacity, volume, and size DO remain part of identity: REJECT mini/travel sizes, different capacities, bundles that include other products, other models or lines from the same brand, and counterfeit or replica versions.
Condition: reject ONLY if the listing explicitly states used, refurbished, pre-owned, or for-parts. Do NOT infer condition from photos or terse titles. When a marketplace-stated condition is provided, trust it: 'Open box' / 'New other' / no-box / damaged-box grades mean a NEW item and are acceptable.
Return ONLY JSON: {"verdict": "ACCEPT" or "REJECT", "pack_count": <TOTAL number of identical base units in the candidate listing, counted in the same base unit as the reference — e.g. 2 for a 2-pack; a listing of 4 packs of 500 swabs against a 500-count reference is 2000; null if unclear>, "reason": "<20 words"}

protocol.output_cap: up to 10 listings per task (extras truncated)
protocol.invocations: one invocation per task, no agent re-attempts; a single transport-level retry is allowed only when the vendor API 5xxs before producing any output
protocol.tool_config: claude: web_search_20260209 + web_fetch_20260209, max_uses 12 each, pause_turn continuation cap 8; openai: web_search; gemini: google_search grounding; perplexity: Agent API built-in search, preset=high, real image input (normalized base64 data URI); findcheap: /search as shipped (exact track: exact_brand=True)
protocol.image_transport: product image attached as base64 of the harness-normalized image (retailer CDNs bot-wall URL fetchers)
protocol.max_execution: findcheap 360s HTTP timeout; baselines 600s HTTP timeout per call
protocol.geography: US retailers, US-shippable; buyer location for calculated shipping pinned to ZIP 10001 (a generic major-metro US ZIP with no personal association; manual checks enter the same ZIP in retailer shipping estimators; calculated shipping varies by destination, disclosed in limitations)
protocol.shipping_basis: non-Prime / no membership programs (2026-08-29 ruling, consistent with the no-membership-prices rule): Amazon >= $35 ships free, under $35 resolved by manual logged-out checks at ZIP 10001 in the pre-run reference-shipping pass, which pins every reference's non-deterministic shipping BEFORE searches; a Prime counterfactual (all Amazon shipping $0, ~75% of US Amazon shoppers have Prime) is reported separately
protocol.transport: the claude searcher column runs through the Message Batches API (2026-08-28) — identical model/tools/prompts, tokens billed at 50% batch rates (per-search fees unchanged); chosen over halving that column's N, which would have thinned the pooled oracle on the skipped tasks and broken column comparability. Its per-task latency is not measurable under batch scheduling (latency_s=null; the rehearsal's interactive medians are the cited latency figures). The batch analog of the single transport-level retry re-submits errored/expired batch results once. All other columns are interactive HTTP
protocol.pack_normalization: multi-pack references (2026-08-26): candidates with different pack counts qualify on the equivalence track and are scored on landed price PER UNIT — (item + mandatory shipping) / pack count — matching production's price-per-count display; the exact track still requires the same count
protocol.shipping_policies: hard-coded published thresholds (2026-08-26): Amazon/Walmart/Target/Best Buy free >= $35 (under: Walmart $6.99, Target $5.99, Amazon/Best Buy vary); Kohl's free >= $49 else $8.95; Macy's free >= $49; Chewy free >= $49 else $4.99; Shein free >= $29; Sephora free >= $50; Apple and Nordstrom always free
protocol.shipping: LANDED COST (2026-08-25): 'cheaper' = item price + mandatory shipping for a single-item order to a US address, no paid memberships. Shipping resolves via the locked retailer policy table, then human verification; agent-reported shipping used elsewhere; unknown shipping resolved at the price frontier (R&D: human audit; final run: automated page-text extraction). The REFERENCE is landed too: origin page's item price + its own mandatory shipping under the same rules.
protocol.discounts: no coupons, promo codes, membership-gated prices, or first-order/new-customer WELCOME prices (AliExpress/Temu/Shein-style) — the basis is the standing price available to any shopper
protocol.findcheap_prices: Findcheap item prices are vendor-API sourced and treated as verified; its shipping and stock are audited like everyone else's

meta.shipping_basis: non-Prime / no membership programs; ref shipping pre-verified (--ref-shipping: locked policy table, else manual logged-out check at ZIP 10001)
